title: Charge-Sector Construction of the Type-IIB Axion--Dilaton Wormhole Partition Function
abstract: I construct the Type-IIB axion--dilaton wormhole partition function from charge-sector data. In a chosen axion charge, equivalently form-field flux sector, the long-distance saddle calculation supplies a two-end operator term with coefficient matrix \(C^{ij}_ν\). The labels \(i,j\) label end-insertion operators; the labels \(A,B\) label parent universes. Reduction data \(b\) convert this matrix into scalar coefficients \(W_ν[b]\). The wormhole partition function in the theta variable is \(Z_{\rm wh}(θ;b)=\sum_νW_ν[b]\e^{iνθ}\). I analyze properties and constraints this coefficients satisfy: discrete-symmetry covariance, phase, absolute bounds, moment positivity, Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities for the unreduced coefficient matrix, complex-\(θ\) domains, charge-lattice tails, and the dilute Bessel/Skellam limit. The \(θ\)-dependence of the wormhole partition function is the Fourier transform of the charge-sector scalar coefficients.
summary: This paper constructs the partition function for a Type-IIB axion--dilaton wormhole using charge-sector data. It develops a sophisticated mathematical framework to analyze this function via its $	heta$-expansion coefficients. The core contribution is establishing necessary and sufficient conditions—such as positivity or symmetry—that these coefficients must satisfy to correspond to physically meaningful quantities.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing the Type-IIB axion--dilaton wormhole partition function, Z_wh(theta; b), entirely from underlying charge-sector data.
main_result: The paper establishes a rigorous mathematical framework detailing how physical constraints (like positivity or symmetry) on the coefficient sequence dictate the nature of the theta expansion, connecting it to known statistical distributions like Bessel/Skellam laws.
method: The method involves deriving coefficients from long-distance saddle point calculations in supergravity, followed by a reduction procedure that maps these matrix elements into scalar coefficients forming a Fourier series representation for Z_wh.
